title: Repository access
subtitle: Tokens and keys Studio uses to connect to GitHub, GitLab and other servers.

credentials.title: Tokens and keys
credentials.empty: No access yet. It appears when you connect a repository.

hosts.title: Trusted servers
hosts.empty: No servers yet. A server key is remembered after you confirm it.

secrets.title: Secret storage
secrets.ok: Secrets are stored encrypted in the Studio data folder.
secrets.unavailable: The secret store is unavailable: tokens cannot be saved.
secrets.sharedFolder: The data folder is inside a cloud drive ({{provider}}). Encrypted tokens and the encryption key will end up in the cloud.

secretsUnavailable: The secret store is unavailable: tokens and keys cannot be saved. Check the Studio data folder.

mismatch.sshOnHttps: A key works only with an ssh address, but an https address was entered.
mismatch.tokenOnSsh: A token works only with an https address, but an ssh address was entered.

pat.stored: The token is stored encrypted on this computer and is never shown again.
pat.label: Access name
pat.usernameHint: Only needed for servers that ask for a name together with the token. Usually left empty.

ssh.emptyTitle: There is no key for this server yet
ssh.emptyText: Studio will create a key on this computer. The private part stays here, and you add the public part to the repository.
ssh.allowWrite: Do not forget to allow write access for the key (Allow write access): with read-only access versions cannot be sent.

browser.title: Sign in with the browser
browser.text: GitHub and GitLab without tokens or keys
browser.tooltip: Sign-in without tokens is coming later

fix.useBound: Update the access the project is connected with

help.tokenNote: Give the token only the permissions it needs and an expiry date: you can revoke it in the server settings.
help.keyNote: The private part of the key stays on this computer and is never sent anywhere.

token.open: On GitHub open Settings, Developer settings, Fine-grained tokens and click Generate new token.
token.repo: Under Repository access choose Only select repositories and tick this repository.
token.perm: Under Permissions, Repository permissions set Contents: Read and write.
token.copy: Click Generate token and copy the value: GitHub shows it only once.

key.open: Open the repository's Deploy keys page (button below) and click Add deploy key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Tick Allow write access: without it the repository accepts the key for reading only.

token.open: Open Preferences, Access tokens and click Add new token.
token.scope: Tick the write_repository scope (it includes reading) and role Developer or higher.
token.copy: Create the token and copy the value: GitLab shows it only once.

key.open: Open the repository's Settings, Repository, Deploy keys and click Add new key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Turn on Grant write permissions to this key.

token.open: Open Settings, Applications and find the access tokens section.
token.perm: Give the token the repository: Read and write permission.
token.copy: Create the token and copy the value: it will not be shown later.

key.open: Open the repository's Settings, Deploy Keys and click Add Deploy Key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Turn on Enable Write Access: otherwise versions cannot be sent.

token.open: Open Personal settings, App passwords and create an app password.
token.perm: Give it the Repositories: Write permission.
token.copy: Copy the password and paste it here as the token: Bitbucket shows it only once.

key.open: Open the repository's Repository settings, Access keys and click Add key.
key.paste: Paste the public key from the field above, any title.
key.write: Sending versions needs write access: if a Bitbucket repository key is read-only, add the key to your profile under Personal settings, SSH keys.

token.create: Open your profile settings on the server and create a personal access token with write permission for the repository.
token.copy: Copy the value and paste it above: the server usually shows it only once.

key.paste: Add the public key from the field above to the repository settings or your profile on the server.
key.write: Allow the key to write: a read-only key cannot send versions.

hostKey.unknownText: Studio will remember the server key and recognize it later: this way an impostor server does not get your data. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server publishes and confirm.
hostKey.changedText: The server used to present a different key. The connection is stopped.
hostKey.changedWarning: This may be a server impersonation. If the administrator changed the key on purpose, compare the new fingerprint with the one they published and only then replace the key.
hostKey.typeHost: To replace the key, type the server name: {{host}}
hostKey.whereToCheck: You can compare the fingerprint on the server's page with its ssh keys or with its administrator. If it does not match, decline.
hostKey.failed: Could not remember the server key.
hostKey.revealing: Fetching the fingerprint of the new key…
hostKey.revealFailed: Could not get the new server key fingerprint. The key cannot be replaced blindly.
hostKey.noFingerprint: The new fingerprint is not known yet, the key was not replaced.

credentials.openProject: Open the sync settings of the project “{{name}}”
credentials.authFailedHint: The server did not accept this access. Replace the token or the key.

replaceDialog.title: Replace token
replaceDialog.description: The new token replaces the old one for {{host}}. You can revoke the old token in the server settings.
replaceDialog.keepHint: The token is stored encrypted on this computer and is never shown again.

deleteDialog.title: Delete the access “{{label}}”?
deleteDialog.description: The token or key is erased from the Studio and cannot be restored.
deleteDialog.usedText: Syncing in them stops until you set a new access.
deleteDialog.confirmUsed: Delete and leave the projects without access

hosts.intro: Servers whose keys you confirmed for ssh. If a server key changes, the Studio stops the connection and asks you.
hosts.forgetText: Next time you connect, the Studio shows the key fingerprint again and you have to confirm it.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.sourceFile: The encryption key is in a file in the Studio data folder.
encryption.sourceEnv: The encryption key comes from an environment variable and is not in the data folder.
encryption.permissionsOk: The key file is closed to other users of this computer.
encryption.permissionsNotEnforced: The key file is not closed to other users: the system does not let us restrict permissions. Do not give strangers access to the data folder.
encryption.unreadable_one: {{count}} access could not be read: the encryption key was lost or replaced. Enter this token again.
encryption.unreadable_other: {{count}} accesses could not be read: the encryption key was lost or replaced. Enter these tokens again.
encryption.unavailableText: The secret store is unavailable: tokens and keys cannot be saved. Check the Studio data folder and its permissions.
encryption.sharedFolder: The data folder is inside a cloud drive ({{provider}}), so the encrypted tokens and the encryption key go to the cloud together and the encryption protects almost nothing. Move the key file outside the drive: the path is set by the HSE_STUDIO__SECRETS__KEY_FILE variable.
encryption.threat: Encryption protects against accidental leaks: a copy of the data folder, a cloud drive, a screenshot. It does not protect against malware on this computer or against someone who holds the whole data folder together with the key.

fetchDefault.title: Default background check
fetchDefault.text: How often the Studio checks project repositories in the background. You can change it for a single project in its sync settings. This setting is personal and is not shared with colleagues.
fetchDefault.label: Default interval

none.hint: Public repositories are cloned without a token. For a private repository, choose a token or a key.
